Pure lunar calendars have twelve lunar months invariantly and consequently their New Year is not fixed relative to the solar year; no adjustments are made. In contrast, most lunisolar calendars also have twelve lunar months, but every few years, a thirteenth "leap month" is added to resynchronise with the solar year.

The determination of the first day of a new lunar year or lunisolar year varies by culture. The event is celebrated by numerous cultures in various ways at different dates.
